source_text: Spe malo carendi ad fidei praesidia convolamus, non autem caremus innatis: siquidem post Baptisma virilitas ipsa perdurat Tolle exempli causam, tolletur et pretii, quod pro nobis factus est
pass_a_gloss: Spe to-evil carendi to of-faith praesidia convolamus, not however caremus innatis: siquidem after baptism virilitas herself perdurat Tolle exempli case, tolletur and pretii, that/which for to-us made is.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Remove the reason of his example, and you will also remove the reason for his becoming a ransom for us.
We hurry to faith’s defenses in the hope of being free from evil. Yet we do not become free from what is inborn: male sexual capacity itself remains after baptism.

choices.why: Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.
Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
